summary: Blocking issue found in UserScopedCacheTrait::getCacheKeyParameters(): the APICacheException constructor is called with only 2 arguments, passing the int error-code constant as the second argument (string $developerInfo). This means: (a) with strict_types=1 declared in UserScopedCacheTrait.php, PHP 8.4 will throw a TypeError instead of APICacheException at runtime; (b) even without strict_types, the exception code would be 0 — not ERROR_EMPTY_USER_CACHE_IDENTIFIER — violating AC #4. This bug was not caught by PHPStan because the trait.unused suppression prevents analysis of the trait's method bodies when there is no consumer class. Fix: add an explicit empty-string (or useful developer detail string) as the second argument, and pass the error code as the third argument. The union-operator fix from the previous rework is correctly implemented and confirmed. All other aspects of the implementation are high quality.

Non-blocking items carried forward: (1) whitespace-only identifier passes the guard — acceptable for internal library code, (2) phpstan.neon trait.unused suppression must be removed by WP-004/WP-005 when the first consumer is added, (3) a UserScopedCacheTraitTest.php covering empty-identifier throwing, _userScope injection, and union-operator precedence would be valuable before consumer WPs close.

comments.note:
BLOCKING — APICacheException constructor called with wrong argument positions in UserScopedCacheTrait::getCacheKeyParameters() (UserScopedCacheTrait.php line 55).

Current (broken):
  throw new APICacheException(
      'User-scoped cache method returned an empty user identifier.',
      APICacheException::ERROR_EMPTY_USER_CACHE_IDENTIFIER
  );

Application_Exception.__construct signature:
  (string $message, string $developerInfo = '', int $code = 0, ?Throwable $previous = null)

The int constant 59213009 is passed as arg #2 ($developerInfo: string). Two consequences:
  1. With declare(strict_types=1) present in UserScopedCacheTrait.php: PHP 8.4 throws TypeError instead of APICacheException — the wrong exception type is raised entirely.
  2. Without strict_types coercion: APICacheException IS thrown, but getCode() returns 0, not ERROR_EMPTY_USER_CACHE_IDENTIFIER — directly violating AC #4.

Additional context: the trait.unused PHPStan suppression prevents analysis of the trait's method bodies when no consumer exists, so this was silently missed by the static analysis pass.

Fix — use the standard 3-argument form, consistent with APICacheManager.php:
  throw new APICacheException(
      'User-scoped cache method returned an empty user identifier.',
      sprintf('Class [%s] returned an empty identifier from getUserCacheIdentifier().', get_class($this)),
      APICacheException::ERROR_EMPTY_USER_CACHE_IDENTIFIER
  );

Note: get_class($this) is safe inside a trait method and provides actionable developer diagnostics.
